claims.explanation: Piperacetazine is a phenothiazine antipsychotic that, beyond dopamine receptor antagonism, directly binds and inhibits the PAX3::FOXO1 fusion protein and inhibits squalene epoxidase (SQLE), disrupting cholesterol/lipid metabolism. The selective killing pattern is best explained by sensitivity of lines with high SQLE/cholesterol-pathway dependence and RAS/RTK-MAPK-driven tumors (NRAS, KRAS, EGFR, BRAF mutations), which are known to be vulnerable to lipid-metabolic and fusion-protein/transcriptional perturbation, while lines with intact PTEN/PI3K-AKT signaling and low proliferative/lipid demand are relatively protected.

features.basis: Piperacetazine is a competitive SQLE inhibitor; high SQLE expression predicts greater dependence and drug effect
NRAS-mutant lines (BFTC905, SW1088, SNU719, KU1919) are enriched among selectively killed lines
KRAS-mutant lines (LU99, SW1573, SNU410, LS1034) are enriched among selectively killed lines
EGFR-mutant lines (KNS81, HCC4006) are selectively killed; EGFR signaling links to lipid metabolism
BRAF-mutant lines (HS939T, 8305C) are selectively killed, consistent with MAPK-driven lipid dependence
PTEN-mutant lines appear in both groups but several least-affected lines carry PTEN loss, suggesting context-dependent protection
TP53 mutation is common across selectively killed lines, though not specific
PAX3::FOXO1 fusion is directly bound and inhibited by piperacetazine in alveolar RMS
PAX3::FOXO1 fusion protein inhibition by piperacetazine reduces oncogenic transcription
Annotated dopamine receptor antagonist activity; DRD2-expressing lines may be more responsive
ARID1A mutations appear in several selectively killed lines (SW1088, KU1919) but also in protected lines, weak evidence
CDKN2A loss appears in several least-affected lines, suggesting reduced sensitivity
